title: Java: 1,000,000 rows
dataset: 10 columns per row: integers, strings (one unique per row), floats, a date/time and a boolean, written to a discarding stream
method: Stopwatch runner: mean of 5 runs after 2 warm-ups, bytes allocated by the writing thread per run. Peak RSS from a separate single run in a fresh JVM with default settings that creates the rows on demand; creating the rows without writing anything peaks at 314 MB.
notes: At the same deflate level Hypaxel is about 2.5 to 3x faster than FastExcel. FastExcel's own default is a higher level, which makes its files smaller than at level 1 but still larger than Hypaxel's.

At level 6 Hypaxel is slower than FastExcel at level 1 and produces a file less than half the size. About 70% of Hypaxel's time at level 1 is spent in the JDK's Deflater, so the compression level decides most of the run time.
Peak RSS is dominated by the JVM and by garbage between collections, not by what a writer keeps alive. All three writers stream; FastExcel was flushed every 100 rows and POI used a 100-row window.
Allocation does not grow with the row count for the typed, RowWriter and object-mapping paths. addRow(Object...) boxes its arguments, and shared strings keep every distinct string.
FastExcel needs a style per date cell to show dates as dates; that call is part of its loop.
The machine was running other work (load average about 10); treat differences of a few percent as noise.
